hero.headline: U.S. launches second round of strikes on Iran in three days
hero.body:
The United States has conducted a second round of military strikes against Iranian targets within three days, according to officials. The attacks come as diplomatic negotiations between Washington and Tehran continue amid an ongoing conflict.

President Trump indicated that talks with Iran have been productive, announcing he would pause U.S. strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure for five days pending the success of ongoing discussions. Despite this announcement, Israeli forces launched a separate wave of strikes on Iranian targets in Tehran shortly afterward, according to statements from the Israeli Defense Forces.

The Israeli military said it struck military bases, weapons sites, and facilities operated by the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps. The IDF stated it would continue operations according to directives from Israel's political leadership. An Israeli Defense Ministry official told reporters that energy infrastructure would be spared from targeting, aligning with the U.S. decision to hold back strikes on power plants and related sites.

Reports indicate the scale of explosions in Tehran was substantial. An Al Jazeera correspondent described the volume of blasts as "unprecedented."

The human toll from the broader conflict continues to mount. The U.S.-based Human Rights Activists News Agency recorded at least 206 attacks across 15 Iranian provinces in a 24-hour period, resulting in at least four casualties. According to various estimates, total fatalities from the conflict have surpassed 1,500, with some rights groups reporting figures as high as 3,230. At least 15 percent of total casualties have been children.

The Israeli military reported destroying or rendering inoperable approximately 330 of Iran's estimated 470 ballistic missile launchers since the conflict began. More than half were hit in airstrikes, while others were disabled through attacks on storage site entrances. Missile fire on Israel has decreased to approximately 10 attacks daily, down from roughly 90 at the conflict's start.

Beyond Iran, hostilities continue in other locations. Israeli forces conducted strikes on Beirut's southern suburbs, the first attacks on the Hezbollah stronghold in several days. Lebanon's health ministry reported one death from the strikes. Israel also announced it had captured two members of the Iranian-backed group in southern Lebanon.

Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called for the annexation of areas in southern Lebanon, stating that Israel should "apply sovereignty" over controlled territory. He indicated the military campaign should end with what he described as "a different reality entirely," including shifting Israel's borders to the Litani River.

The escalation of military activity occurs despite ongoing ceasefire frameworks and negotiations aimed at reaching a permanent resolution to the three-month conflict between the United States and Iran.

cards.headline: Paper mill explosion in Longview could be Washington's deadliest industrial disaster
cards.teaser: A disaster at a Longview paper mill may become the deadliest industrial tragedy in modern Washington state history, the governor said.
cards.body:
Washington's governor said an explosion at a paper mill in Longview could rank as the state's deadliest industrial accident in modern history. A tank ruptured at the Nippon Dynawave Packaging Co facility on Tuesday morning, killing at least two people and leaving nine others missing and presumed dead. Nine additional people were injured in the incident.

The disaster involved a chemical tank at the paper mill. Authorities have transitioned from rescue to recovery operations as they work to account for all those affected by the explosion.

cards.headline: Justice Department opens criminal investigation into Trump accuser E. Jean Carroll
cards.body:
The Department of Justice has opened a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll, who accused President Trump of sexual assault, according to multiple reports. CNN first reported the investigation Wednesday night.

The probe focuses on whether Carroll committed perjury during a deposition as part of her two civil cases against Trump. Carroll won those civil cases, in which juries found Trump liable for sexual abuse and defamation.

The investigation represents a significant shift in the Justice Department's handling of matters related to Trump and his accusers. Carroll's legal victories against Trump in civil court resulted in substantial monetary damages.

The timing of the investigation has drawn attention, coming years after Carroll first publicly accused Trump of assault in the 1990s at a New York department store. Trump has repeatedly denied the allegations.

Carroll's attorney has not publicly commented on the reported investigation. The Justice Department typically does not confirm or deny ongoing investigations.

The perjury investigation appears to center on statements Carroll made under oath during depositions in her defamation and battery lawsuits against Trump. Those cases proceeded through federal court in New York.

The civil trials featured testimony from Carroll and other witnesses, along with evidence presented by both legal teams. Juries in both cases ruled in Carroll's favor, awarding her millions of dollars in damages.

The criminal investigation marks a new legal front in the long-running dispute between Carroll and Trump. Perjury charges require prosecutors to prove that a person knowingly made false statements under oath with intent to deceive.

Federal perjury cases can be difficult to prosecute, as they require clear evidence that the defendant deliberately lied rather than simply misremembered or misspoke. The Justice Department has not indicated what specific statements might be under scrutiny.

cards.headline: Uganda Closes Border With Congo as Ebola Cases Rise
cards.teaser: Uganda shut its border with the Democratic Republic of Congo after seven confirmed Ebola cases were reported in the capital.
cards.body:
Uganda closed its border with the Democratic Republic of Congo as Ebola cases continue to surge in the region. Seven confirmed cases have been reported in Kampala, Uganda's capital, prompting officials to implement this significant containment measure.

The outbreak in eastern DRC has grown substantially, with authorities reporting over 900 suspected cases and 119 suspected deaths. Uganda has activated its disease surveillance systems to monitor the situation. The border closure mirrors restrictions used during previous health crises to prevent the virus from spreading across borders.

cards.headline: Former CIA officer arrested with $40 million in gold bars at home
cards.teaser: Federal authorities arrested a former CIA official after discovering 300 gold bars worth approximately $40 million in his residence.
cards.body:
The FBI arrested David Rush, a former U.S. government official who previously worked for the CIA, after finding $40 million worth of gold bars in his home. Prosecutors allege Rush stole 300 gold bars from the agency.

The arrest marks a major case of alleged theft from within the intelligence community. The Justice Department has charged Rush in connection with the seized gold, though the timeline of the alleged theft has not been disclosed.

cards.headline: Google Engineer Charged With Insider Trading Over $1.2M in Polymarket Bets
cards.body:
A Google engineer faces federal insider trading charges after prosecutors allege he used confidential company information to make $1.2 million betting on Polymarket.

The longtime Google employee was charged in New York for allegedly violating insider trading laws. According to prosecutors, the engineer worked in information security at Google and used inside information to place bets on the prediction market platform.

The case centers on allegations that the engineer exploited access to internal Google data to gain an unfair advantage when placing bets. Prosecutors claim he wagered on search terms using confidential information obtained through his position at the company.

Polymarket is a cryptocurrency-based prediction market where users bet on the outcomes of future events. The platform has grown in popularity for betting on everything from political elections to sports outcomes and market trends.

The engineer's role in information security would have given him access to sensitive internal data at Google. Federal prosecutors allege he used this privileged access to identify betting opportunities on Polymarket that other users could not see.

Insider trading laws traditionally apply to stock markets, where trading on material nonpublic information is illegal. This case represents an application of those laws to the emerging world of prediction markets, where real money changes hands based on the outcomes of future events.

The $1.2 million in alleged profits came from bets the engineer placed using the confidential Google information, according to the charges filed in New York. The specific search terms or data he allegedly used were not detailed in the available information about the case.

The charges highlight the legal risks facing employees at technology companies who have access to valuable internal data. As prediction markets grow in size and sophistication, prosecutors appear willing to pursue cases involving the misuse of corporate information on these platforms.

Google has not commented on the charges against its employee. The case is being prosecuted in New York, where federal authorities have aggressively pursued insider trading cases across various markets.

cards.headline: Packers Running Back Josh Jacobs Released From Jail, District Attorney Delays Charging Decision
cards.body:
Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs was released from jail after his arrest on domestic violence charges. The district attorney has not yet decided whether to file formal charges against the player.

Jacobs faced arrest on five charges, including felony strangulation, according to reports. The charges stem from an alleged domestic violence incident, though specific details about what occurred have not been disclosed publicly.

The Packers player was taken into custody and later released as the investigation continues. Law enforcement has not provided a timeline for when the district attorney's office will make a decision on whether to proceed with charges.

The felony strangulation charge represents the most serious allegation among the five charges Jacobs faced at the time of his arrest. Such charges typically carry significant legal consequences if prosecutors decide to move forward.

Jacobs joined the Packers and has been a key part of the team's backfield. His legal situation now creates uncertainty about his status with the franchise as the investigation unfolds.

The district attorney's office is reviewing evidence and determining whether sufficient grounds exist to formally charge Jacobs. This review process can take days or weeks depending on the complexity of the case and the evidence available to prosecutors.

Neither Jacobs nor his representatives have issued public statements about the arrest or the allegations. The Packers organization has also not commented on the situation or indicated what steps, if any, they plan to take regarding Jacobs' status with the team.

Domestic violence cases involving professional athletes often draw significant public attention and can result in league discipline separate from any criminal proceedings. The NFL has not announced whether it will conduct its own investigation into the matter.

The investigation remains active as authorities continue gathering information. Jacobs' release from jail does not indicate the outcome of the case, as prosecutors frequently release individuals while deciding whether to file charges.

cards.headline: Iran Restores Internet Access After 88-Day Shutdown
cards.teaser: The Iranian government is allowing citizens to reconnect with the world after a near-total internet blackout lasting nearly three months.
cards.body:
Iran has begun restoring internet access following an 88-day period of censored news, television, and chat services. The government imposed the near-total internet shutdown during the conflict with the United States.

Not everyone in Iran has regained access to online services. Those who have reconnected are uncertain how long the restored access will last, as the government maintains control over network availability.

cards.headline: Record Spring Heat Wave Breaks Temperatures Across Europe
cards.teaser: An exceptionally early heat wave has shattered records and caused deaths in multiple European countries.
cards.body:
Western Europe is experiencing an exceptionally early spring heat wave, with temperatures shattering records across multiple major capitals. London has reached 95 degrees for two consecutive days, and the extreme conditions have triggered government warnings across the continent.

Experts warn that unpredictable and extreme weather events are becoming increasingly frequent. The heat wave underscores growing concerns about the escalating severity of weather patterns worldwide.

cards.headline: Snowflake and Amazon Announce $6 Billion Cloud Computing Deal
cards.teaser: The data company will spend $6 billion on Amazon's cloud services to support enterprise AI adoption.
cards.body:
Snowflake has committed $6 billion to Amazon Web Services over five years to secure specialized AI computing chips. The deal strengthens their existing partnership and aims to support enterprise demand for agentic AI infrastructure.

The announcement drove Snowflake's stock up 36 percent, bolstered by an earnings beat and raised sales guidance. The company cited growing AI demand as a key factor in its business outlook.

cards.headline: Australia Sues 3M for $2 Billion Over PFAS Contamination at Defense Sites
cards.teaser: The Australian government filed suit against the US manufacturer over chemicals in firefighting foam.
cards.body:
Australia's government has filed a $2 billion lawsuit against 3M, seeking damages to cover costs related to PFAS contamination at 28 defense bases. The case involves firefighting foam containing "forever chemicals" that the government says caused widespread environmental damage across the country's military sites.

PFAS chemicals do not break down naturally and persist in the environment indefinitely. The contamination at defense facilities has raised significant health and environmental concerns, prompting the government's legal action to recover costs associated with addressing the contamination.

cards.headline: California court rejects Tesla's motion to dismiss racial discrimination lawsuit
cards.teaser: A California court denied Tesla's attempt to throw out a racial discrimination lawsuit filed by the state's civil rights agency.
cards.body:
California defeated Tesla's motion to dismiss a racial discrimination lawsuit brought by the state's civil rights agency. The agency celebrated the court decision and said it anticipates a trial in July.

The lawsuit was filed by California's civil rights enforcement agency against the electric vehicle manufacturer. The court's ruling allows the case to proceed to trial, where the agency will present evidence related to its discrimination claims against Tesla.

cards.headline: Senate Bill Proposes College Sports Salary Cap and Transfer Limits
cards.teaser: Senators Ted Cruz and Maria Cantwell introduced bipartisan legislation to reform college athletics with new restrictions on player movement and compensation.
cards.body:
Senators Ted Cruz and Maria Cantwell have introduced a bipartisan bill addressing college sports reform. The legislation proposes a salary cap for athletes and limits on transfers, representing a significant intervention in how college athletics operate.

The bill seeks to enforce caps on athlete compensation and restrict how often players can transfer between schools. The legislation also targets coaching moves, specifically addressing situations like Lane Kiffin's recent jump to LSU. SEC leaders are discussing backup plans as the bill moves through Congress.

cards.headline: Lebanon Braces for Prolonged War Despite U.S.-Iran Negotiations
cards.teaser: Lebanese citizens expect fighting to continue even if the United States and Iran reach a diplomatic agreement.
cards.body:
Few people in Lebanon believe that diplomatic efforts to end the wider war will bring peace to their country. Clashes between Israel and Hezbollah have intensified in southern Lebanon even as negotiations continue to address the broader conflict.

The pessimism reflects a disconnect between regional diplomacy and local dynamics on the Lebanese-Israeli border. Residents have resigned themselves to continued fighting regardless of any agreement reached between the parties involved in the larger conflict.

cards.headline: Republicans reconcile with Paxton after Texas Senate primary defeat of Cornyn
cards.teaser: Senate Republicans are working to repair relationships with Ken Paxton following a contentious Texas primary that unseated an incumbent.
cards.body:
The Texas Republican primary runoff has concluded, setting major matchups for November. After a contentious race, Republican senators are beginning to reconcile with Ken Paxton following his victory over incumbent John Cornyn in the primary.

Democrats are assessing their prospects against Paxton in the general election for the Texas Senate seat. The primary outcome marks a significant shift in Texas politics and has prompted analysis of the Republican Party's direction moving forward.

cards.headline: Federal Court Orders Customs Chief to Address Tariff Refund Compliance
cards.teaser: A judge demanded the customs commissioner appear at a hearing about repaying $166 billion in illegally imposed tariffs.
cards.body:
A federal court ordered the head of US Customs to appear at a hearing to address compliance with requirements to refund tariffs ruled illegal. The order represents new concern about the Trump administration's efforts to repay the full $166 billion owed from the tariffs.

The court's demand for the customs chief to appear in person signals judicial scrutiny of the refund process. The tariffs at issue were previously determined to have been illegally imposed, creating a legal obligation to return the money collected.

cards.headline: Rivian sets June 9 delivery date for first R2 SUVs
cards.teaser: Rivian announced it will deliver the first R2 SUVs to customers on June 9, marking a key launch for the electric vehicle maker.
cards.body:
Rivian will deliver the first R2 SUVs on June 9. CEO RJ Scaringe has described the R2 launch as "maybe the most important thing we've launched to date," underscoring the vehicle's significance for the company's future.

The R2 represents a key expansion of Rivian's vehicle lineup as it moves beyond its initial R1T truck and R1S SUV models.

cards.headline: Spielberg Says Hollywood Should Never Use AI as Final Word on Creative Decisions
cards.body:
Steven Spielberg spoke against using artificial intelligence in filmmaking during a recent appearance on Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson's IMO podcast. The director drew a clear line on where he believes AI should and should not be applied in creative industries.

Spielberg said he sees value in AI for solving medical problems but opposes its use in taking over the creative process in Hollywood. He stated that Hollywood should never use AI as the final word on anything creative, describing that as where he draws the line.

The director's comments add his voice to ongoing debates in the entertainment industry about the role of artificial intelligence in creative work. His position focuses on maintaining human control over artistic decisions while acknowledging potential benefits of AI in other fields.

Spielberg has directed numerous films over a career spanning more than five decades. His stance reflects concerns among many filmmakers about preserving human creativity and decision-making in an industry increasingly exploring technological tools.

The podcast appearance with Obama and Robinson provided a platform for Spielberg to address technology's expanding role in entertainment. His remarks specifically targeted the use of AI in creative decision-making rather than as a support tool.

The director's position distinguishes between AI applications he considers acceptable and those he views as crossing a boundary. He emphasized that creative choices should remain in human hands even as technology offers new capabilities to the film industry.

cards.headline: Student Criticizes CBS News While Accepting Mike Wallace Scholarship
cards.teaser: A scholarship winner used his acceptance speech at the News Emmys to publicly challenge CBS News direction.
cards.body:
Santiago Campos, a senior at District of Columbia International School in Washington, used his acceptance speech for the Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship at the News Emmys to criticize CBS News. He told the assembled audience that the network's recent direction undermines the legacy of the legendary journalist the scholarship commemorates.

Former CBS Evening News anchor Scott Pelley presented the award to Campos during the ceremony.

cards.headline: US military shoots down four Iranian drones, strikes launch site
cards.teaser: American forces intercepted drones targeting a commercial ship in the Strait of Hormuz and destroyed a ground control station.
cards.body:
The U.S. military intercepted four Iranian attack drones threatening a commercial vessel in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday and destroyed an Iranian ground control station in Bandar Abbas that was preparing to launch a fifth drone. U.S. Central Command confirmed the military action.

This marks the second such confrontation in 48 hours between the two nations. The incidents occur amid ongoing negotiations to end the three-month conflict and a fragile ceasefire between the U.S. and Iran.

cards.headline: Former judges ask court to investigate Trump IRS settlement
cards.teaser: A bipartisan group of former federal judges filed a request to reopen Trump's lawsuit against the tax agency.
cards.body:
A bipartisan group of former federal judges asked a federal court on Wednesday to reopen President Trump's lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service, contending that the administration bypassed judicial oversight by settling the dispute directly.

The $1.776 billion fund created through the settlement compensates alleged victims of what the administration calls "lawfare and weaponization." California Governor Gavin Newsom has announced plans to impose a 100% tax on any payouts received by state residents, seeking to counteract the fund's distribution.

cards.headline: Senator Andy Kim responds to criticism over detention facility protest
cards.teaser: The New Jersey Democrat defended his attendance at a demonstration outside a migrant detention center.
cards.body:
Senator Andy Kim fired back at Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin on Wednesday after Mullin criticized the senator for attending a protest outside a migrant detention facility in New Jersey. Kim said the issue was never about him personally.

During a cabinet meeting at the White House on Wednesday, Mullin said Kim complained about being hit by pepper ball spray at the protest. The exchange highlighted tensions between Democratic lawmakers and the Trump administration over immigration enforcement policies.

cards.headline: Zelensky asks Trump and Congress for Patriot missile interceptors
cards.teaser: The Ukrainian president said his country needs anti-missile defense systems to help end the conflict with Russia.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky appealed to President Trump and Congress on Wednesday for Patriot missile interceptors to strengthen Kyiv's air defenses against Russian attacks. Zelensky emphasized that while Ukraine has made progress defending against drone strikes, the country lacks the domestic capability to produce anti-missile defense systems.

The plea comes as Russia continues its assault on Ukrainian targets. Kyiv has achieved some success countering various types of drones but remains dependent on external support for advanced air defense capabilities needed to protect against ongoing Russian strikes.

cards.headline: Jill Biden Says She Feared Husband Was Having Stroke During 2024 Debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady told CBS News she was frightened by Joe Biden's performance against Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Jill Biden told CBS News that she was "frightened" while watching her husband's performance during his 2024 presidential debate against Donald Trump. The former first lady said she had never seen Joe Biden perform that way before or since, and worried he might have suffered a stroke.

Biden's debate performance was widely criticized, and he subsequently lost the 2024 election to Trump, who is now serving his second term in office.

cards.headline: FIFA Faces Investigation Over World Cup Ticket Pricing Practices
cards.teaser: New York and New Jersey are examining whether fans were misled about ticket sales and seating.
cards.body:
Attorneys general from New York and New Jersey have launched an investigation into FIFA's World Cup ticket sales and pricing practices. The probe was triggered by reports that fans were misled about ticket availability and seating information.

Regulators are examining whether FIFA's marketing and sales methods violated consumer protection laws by providing inaccurate details to buyers. The investigation will require FIFA to provide answers regarding its ticketing practices for the 2026 World Cup.

cards.headline: Ferrari's First Electric Car Faces Market Backlash
cards.teaser: The new model drew mockery online, analyst skepticism, and investor selling.
cards.body:
Ferrari's first fully electric vehicle, the Luce model, has triggered sharp criticism following its unveiling. The new model sparked divided reactions on social media, with memes mocking the vehicle. Investors responded negatively, with Ferrari's share price slumping after the announcement.

A former Ferrari chairman warned that the electric vehicle could signal "the destruction of a legend." The backlash reflects concerns about whether an electric Ferrari will appeal to the brand's traditional customer base, as the automaker faces mounting pressure from Chinese EV makers in the market.

cards.headline: NASA spacecraft captures detailed Mars images during flyby
cards.teaser: NASA's Psyche spacecraft photographed Mars in high resolution during a flyby on its journey to a distant asteroid.
cards.body:
NASA's Psyche spacecraft captured detailed images of Mars during a flyby on its journey to a metal-rich asteroid located in the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter. The mission successfully transmitted high-resolution photographs back to Earth, including striking views of Mars' south pole.

The Mars flyby served a dual purpose for the mission, allowing engineers to test the spacecraft's imaging systems while gathering unique perspectives of the red planet. These images represent another milestone in Psyche's extended voyage toward its distant destination.

cards.headline: Dodgers Place Kike Hernandez Back on Injured List With Oblique Tear
cards.teaser: Kike Hernandez returned to the injured list after being diagnosed with a significant oblique tear just two games after his comeback.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Dodgers utility player Kike Hernandez was placed back on the injured list after medical tests revealed a significant oblique tear. The injury occurred just two games after Hernandez returned from a previous stint on the injured list.

Hernandez had made an emotional return to the lineup and contributed to a Dodgers victory over the Colorado Rockies in a seventh-inning surge. The team recalled Freeland from Triple-A to fill the roster spot. The timeline for Hernandez's return has not been announced.

cards.headline: SEC Officials Criticize College Football Playoff Committee's Strength of Schedule Explanation
cards.teaser: Leaders from the Southeastern Conference publicly challenged the College Football Playoff selection committee's methodology for evaluating team schedules.
cards.body:
SEC leaders have voiced strong disagreement with the College Football Playoff committee's explanation of how it measures strength of schedule. The criticism comes as debates intensify over which metrics should determine playoff selections.

The conference officials questioned the transparency and consistency of the committee's process for ranking teams based on their opponents' quality. The dispute reflects ongoing tensions about how the playoff system weighs different conferences and schedules when making its final selections.

cards.headline: Lamar Jackson Says Ravens Coaching Change Feels Like Fresh Start
cards.teaser: The Baltimore quarterback described the team's new coaching staff as reinvigorating and said his commitment to the Ravens remains strong.
cards.body:
Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson said the team's coaching change has brought renewed energy to the organization. Jackson described the transition as feeling like a breath of fresh air while maintaining that his commitment to Baltimore has never wavered.

Jackson declined to discuss ongoing contract negotiations but said he wants to leave the conversation about fully guaranteed contracts in the past. He praised new coordinator Declan Doyle for making his job easier. Jackson also confirmed he remains focused on the Ravens despite questions about his long-term future with the franchise.

cards.headline: ABC News and National Geographic Lead News Emmy Winners
cards.teaser: ABC News won eight awards at the 47th annual News Emmys, with National Geographic close behind at seven wins.
cards.body:
ABC News led all networks at the 47th annual News Emmy Awards with eight wins. The network claimed the top prize for outstanding live news program for ABC World News Tonight With David Muir, repeating its victory from the previous year.

National Geographic won seven News Emmys, with multiple wins for Trafficked With Mariana van Zeller. Both networks are owned by Disney.

cards.headline: Obsession Breaks Box Office Pattern With Second Weekend Increase
cards.teaser: The film achieved a rare second-weekend box office spike, marking an unusual pattern for theatrical releases.
cards.body:
Obsession posted a box office increase in its second weekend of release, a performance pattern described as making history. The film became a breakout box office hit for the summer season.

The second-weekend spike represents a performance not seen since Sound of Freedom. The film's box office trajectory has drawn attention for defying typical weekend-to-weekend decline patterns that most theatrical releases follow.

cards.headline: Morris Day Denies Participation in Freedom 250 National Mall Concert
cards.teaser: The singer said he will not perform at a June concert on the National Mall despite being listed as a headliner by organizers.
cards.body:
Morris Day denied reports that he and the Time will perform at the Freedom 250 concert on the National Mall, calling them rumors. Organizers had announced him as headlining a show scheduled for June 27 as part of a 16-day patriotic fair in Washington.

Day stated it is a no for him regarding the event. The Freedom 250 festival is part of celebrations for the United States' 250th birthday and features other performers including Martina McBride, Flo Rida, and Vanilla Ice.

cards.headline: Donkey Kong 64 joins Nintendo Switch Online next week
cards.teaser: Nintendo will add Donkey Kong 64 to its Nintendo Switch Online N64 library next week.
cards.body:
Nintendo announced that Donkey Kong 64 will join the Nintendo Switch Online service next week, expanding the platform's N64 game library. The 1999 platformer will become available to subscribers with access to the N64 games collection.

Donkey Kong 64 was originally released for the Nintendo 64 console. Nintendo Switch Online offers a subscription service that provides access to classic games from older Nintendo systems, including the N64, Super Nintendo, and NES.

cards.headline: Rodrigo Addresses Criticism Over Recent Fashion Choices
cards.teaser: Olivia Rodrigo responded to online backlash about her clothing, saying people should not be held responsible for others sexualizing them.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo weighed in on controversy surrounding her recent outfits. The singer faced backlash from internet commenters who accused her recent clothing choices of both infantilizing and sexualizing her.

Rodrigo said people should not be responsible for some guy sexualizing them. Her comments addressed the criticism directly as she defended her fashion decisions amid the online debate about her appearance.

hero.headline: U.S. Strikes Iran Military Sites for Second Time in Three Days
hero.body:
The United States conducted strikes against military targets in southern Iran, marking the second round of attacks in three days during a fragile cease-fire. A U.S. official said the strikes were carried out in self-defense and targeted four one-way attack drones and a drone ground-control station.

The attacks threaten ongoing negotiations to end a three-month war between the U.S. and Iran. The cease-fire remains precarious as both sides continue diplomatic efforts while military operations persist.

The official characterized the strikes as defensive measures in response to Iranian military activity. The targets included active attack drones that U.S. forces assessed posed an immediate threat.

President Trump stated he feels no political pressure to reach a deal with Iran, telling reporters Iran is negotiating on fumes. His comments came as the strikes were being carried out, signaling a harder negotiating stance from the administration.

The conflict has now entered its fourth month, with a potential cease-fire still hanging in the balance. Diplomats from both nations have been engaged in protracted negotiations, though the repeated military strikes suggest significant obstacles remain.

The U.S. has now conducted two separate military operations against Iranian targets within a 72-hour period. Both rounds of strikes have been framed by American officials as self-defense actions rather than offensive operations.

The fragile cease-fire has not prevented either side from conducting military operations. The pattern of continued strikes during negotiating periods raises questions about the sustainability of any potential agreement.

Oil markets reacted to the news of fresh strikes, with prices jumping on renewed fears of disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. The strategic waterway remains a key concern for global energy markets as the conflict continues.

cards.headline: Uganda Closes Border With Congo as Ebola Cases Rise
cards.teaser: Uganda shut its border with the Democratic Republic of Congo after seven confirmed Ebola cases were reported in the capital.

cards.headline: Jill Biden Says She Feared Husband Was Having Stroke During 2024 Debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady told CBS News she was frightened by Joe Biden's performance against Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Jill Biden told CBS News that she was "frightened" while watching her husband's performance during his 2024 presidential debate against Donald Trump. The former first lady said she had never seen Joe Biden perform that way before or since, and worried he might have suffered a stroke.

Biden's debate performance was widely criticized, and he subsequently lost the 2024 election to Trump, who is now serving his second term in office.

Lebanon's health ministry reported one death from the strikes. Israel also announced it had captured two members of the Iranian-backed group in southern Lebanon.

Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called for the annexation of areas in southern Lebanon, stating that Israel should "apply sovereignty" over controlled territory. He indicated the military campaign should end with what he described as "a different reality entirely," including shifting Israel's borders to the Litani River.

The escalation of military activity occurs despite ongoing ceasefire frameworks and negotiations aimed at reaching a permanent resolution to the three-month conflict between the United States and Iran.

cards.headline: Former CIA officer arrested with $40 million in gold bars at home
cards.teaser: Federal authorities arrested a former CIA official after discovering 300 gold bars worth approximately $40 million in his residence.
cards.body:
The FBI arrested David Rush, a former U.S. government official who previously worked for the CIA, after finding $40 million worth of gold bars in his home. Prosecutors allege Rush stole 300 gold bars from the agency.

The arrest marks a major case of alleged theft from within the intelligence community. The Justice Department has charged Rush in connection with the seized gold, though the timeline of the alleged theft has not been disclosed.

cards.headline: Paper mill explosion in Longview could be Washington's deadliest industrial disaster
cards.teaser: A disaster at a Longview paper mill may become the deadliest industrial tragedy in modern Washington state history, the governor said.
cards.body:
Washington's governor said an explosion at a paper mill in Longview could rank as the state's deadliest industrial accident in modern history. A tank ruptured at the Nippon Dynawave Packaging Co facility on Tuesday morning, killing at least two people and leaving nine others missing and presumed dead. Nine additional people were injured in the incident.

The disaster involved a chemical tank at the paper mill. Authorities have transitioned from rescue to recovery operations as they work to account for all those affected by the explosion.

cards.headline: Google employee charged with making $1.2 million on insider Polymarket trades
cards.teaser: The Justice Department charged a Google staffer with using insider information to profit from prediction market bets.
cards.body:
Federal prosecutors charged Google engineer Michele Spagnuolo with fraud for allegedly using insider information to profit $1.2 million through Polymarket trades. According to the complaint, Spagnuolo wagered over $2.7 million on bets related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign, leveraging confidential knowledge about search trends before the information became public.

The case marks the second known federal prosecution involving alleged insider trading on a prediction market platform, reflecting growing government scrutiny of these sites as their trading volumes increase.

cards.headline: Republicans reconcile with Paxton after Texas Senate primary defeat of Cornyn
cards.teaser: Senate Republicans are working to repair relationships with Ken Paxton following a contentious Texas primary that unseated an incumbent.
cards.body:
The Texas Republican primary runoff has concluded, setting major matchups for November. After a contentious race, Republican senators are beginning to reconcile with Ken Paxton following his victory over incumbent John Cornyn in the primary.

Democrats are assessing their prospects against Paxton in the general election for the Texas Senate seat. The primary outcome marks a significant shift in Texas politics and has prompted analysis of the Republican Party's direction moving forward.

hero.headline: Google Engineer Charged With Insider Trading Over $1.2M in Polymarket Bets
hero.body:
A Google engineer faces federal insider trading charges after prosecutors allege he used confidential company information to make $1.2 million betting on Polymarket.

The longtime Google employee was charged in New York for allegedly violating insider trading laws. According to prosecutors, the engineer worked in information security at Google and used inside information to place bets on the prediction market platform.

The case centers on allegations that the engineer exploited access to internal Google data to gain an unfair advantage when placing bets. Prosecutors claim he wagered on search terms using confidential information obtained through his position at the company.

Polymarket is a cryptocurrency-based prediction market where users bet on the outcomes of future events. The platform has grown in popularity for betting on everything from political elections to sports outcomes and market trends.

The engineer's role in information security would have given him access to sensitive internal data at Google. Federal prosecutors allege he used this privileged access to identify betting opportunities on Polymarket that other users could not see.

Insider trading laws traditionally apply to stock markets, where trading on material nonpublic information is illegal. This case represents an application of those laws to the emerging world of prediction markets, where real money changes hands based on the outcomes of future events.

The $1.2 million in alleged profits came from bets the engineer placed using the confidential Google information, according to the charges filed in New York. The specific search terms or data he allegedly used were not detailed in the available information about the case.

The charges highlight the legal risks facing employees at technology companies who have access to valuable internal data. As prediction markets grow in size and sophistication, prosecutors appear willing to pursue cases involving the misuse of corporate information on these platforms.

Google has not commented on the charges against its employee. The case is being prosecuted in New York, where federal authorities have aggressively pursued insider trading cases across various markets.

cards.headline: Snowflake and Amazon Announce $6 Billion Cloud Computing Deal
cards.teaser: The data company will spend $6 billion on Amazon's cloud services to support enterprise AI adoption.
cards.body:
Snowflake has committed $6 billion to Amazon Web Services over five years to secure specialized AI computing chips. The deal strengthens their existing partnership and aims to support enterprise demand for agentic AI infrastructure.

The announcement drove Snowflake's stock up 36 percent, bolstered by an earnings beat and raised sales guidance. The company cited growing AI demand as a key factor in its business outlook.

cards.headline: Australia Sues 3M for $2 Billion Over PFAS Contamination at Defense Sites
cards.teaser: The Australian government filed suit against the US manufacturer over chemicals in firefighting foam.
cards.body:
Australia's government has filed a $2 billion lawsuit against 3M, seeking damages to cover costs related to PFAS contamination at 28 defense bases. The case involves firefighting foam containing "forever chemicals" that the government says caused widespread environmental damage across the country's military sites.

PFAS chemicals do not break down naturally and persist in the environment indefinitely. The contamination at defense facilities has raised significant health and environmental concerns, prompting the government's legal action to recover costs associated with addressing the contamination.

cards.headline: Federal Court Orders Customs Chief to Address Tariff Refund Compliance
cards.teaser: A judge demanded the customs commissioner appear at a hearing about repaying $166 billion in illegally imposed tariffs.
cards.body:
A federal court ordered the head of US Customs to appear at a hearing to address compliance with requirements to refund tariffs ruled illegal. The order represents new concern about the Trump administration's efforts to repay the full $166 billion owed from the tariffs.

The court's demand for the customs chief to appear in person signals judicial scrutiny of the refund process. The tariffs at issue were previously determined to have been illegally imposed, creating a legal obligation to return the money collected.

cards.headline: FIFA Faces Investigation Over World Cup Ticket Pricing Practices
cards.teaser: New York and New Jersey are examining whether fans were misled about ticket sales and seating.
cards.body:
Attorneys general from New York and New Jersey have launched an investigation into FIFA's World Cup ticket sales and pricing practices. The probe was triggered by reports that fans were misled about ticket availability and seating information.

Regulators are examining whether FIFA's marketing and sales methods violated consumer protection laws by providing inaccurate details to buyers. The investigation will require FIFA to provide answers regarding its ticketing practices for the 2026 World Cup.

cards.headline: Ferrari's First Electric Car Faces Market Backlash
cards.teaser: The new model drew mockery online, analyst skepticism, and investor selling.
cards.body:
Ferrari's first fully electric vehicle, the Luce model, has triggered sharp criticism following its unveiling. The new model sparked divided reactions on social media, with memes mocking the vehicle. Investors responded negatively, with Ferrari's share price slumping after the announcement.

A former Ferrari chairman warned that the electric vehicle could signal "the destruction of a legend." The backlash reflects concerns about whether an electric Ferrari will appeal to the brand's traditional customer base, as the automaker faces mounting pressure from Chinese EV makers in the market.

hero.headline: Google engineer charged with insider trading after making $1.2 million on Polymarket
hero.body:
A Google engineer faces insider trading charges after making $1.2 million through bets on Polymarket, according to a criminal complaint filed Thursday. The engineer wagered over $2.7 million on predictions related to Google's 2025 Year in Search campaign.

Polymarket is a prediction market platform where users bet on real-world outcomes. The platform gained prominence during recent election cycles but also hosts markets for corporate announcements and cultural events.

The charges center on whether the engineer used nonpublic information from his employment at Google to place informed bets about the company's annual Year in Search results. Google releases this campaign each December, highlighting the year's most popular search queries across various categories.

According to the complaint, the engineer risked more than $2.7 million across multiple wagers, ultimately profiting $1.2 million from the trades. Federal prosecutors allege the engineer had advance knowledge of the campaign's content through his position at the company.

Insider trading laws prohibit trading securities or other financial instruments based on material nonpublic information. While prediction markets occupy a newer regulatory space than traditional stock markets, federal authorities have increasingly scrutinized their use.

The case represents one of the first major insider trading prosecutions tied to prediction market platforms. Legal experts have debated whether existing securities laws fully cover these markets, which allow users to bet on outcomes ranging from election results to corporate decisions.

Google has not commented on the charges or the engineer's employment status. The company maintains strict policies about employees trading on confidential information, whether in traditional markets or newer platforms.

The engineer's name was included in the complaint filed in federal court. If convicted, insider trading charges can carry penalties including prison time and forfeiture of illegal profits. The case will test how courts apply decades-old insider trading statutes to emerging financial technology platforms.

cards.headline: Rivian sets June 9 delivery date for first R2 SUVs
cards.teaser: Rivian announced it will deliver the first R2 SUVs to customers on June 9, marking a key launch for the electric vehicle maker.
cards.body:
Rivian will deliver the first R2 SUVs on June 9. CEO RJ Scaringe has described the R2 launch as "maybe the most important thing we've launched to date," underscoring the vehicle's significance for the company's future.

The R2 represents a key expansion of Rivian's vehicle lineup as it moves beyond its initial R1T truck and R1S SUV models.

cards.headline: California court rejects Tesla's motion to dismiss racial discrimination lawsuit
cards.teaser: A California court denied Tesla's attempt to throw out a racial discrimination lawsuit filed by the state's civil rights agency.
cards.body:
California defeated Tesla's motion to dismiss a racial discrimination lawsuit brought by the state's civil rights agency. The agency celebrated the court decision and said it anticipates a trial in July.

The lawsuit was filed by California's civil rights enforcement agency against the electric vehicle manufacturer. The court's ruling allows the case to proceed to trial, where the agency will present evidence related to its discrimination claims against Tesla.

cards.headline: NASA spacecraft captures detailed Mars images during flyby
cards.teaser: NASA's Psyche spacecraft photographed Mars in high resolution during a flyby on its journey to a distant asteroid.
cards.body:
NASA's Psyche spacecraft captured detailed images of Mars during a flyby on its journey to a metal-rich asteroid located in the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter. The mission successfully transmitted high-resolution photographs back to Earth, including striking views of Mars' south pole.

The Mars flyby served a dual purpose for the mission, allowing engineers to test the spacecraft's imaging systems while gathering unique perspectives of the red planet. These images represent another milestone in Psyche's extended voyage toward its distant destination.

cards.headline: Donkey Kong 64 joins Nintendo Switch Online next week
cards.teaser: Nintendo will add Donkey Kong 64 to its Nintendo Switch Online N64 library next week.
cards.body:
Nintendo announced that Donkey Kong 64 will join the Nintendo Switch Online service next week, expanding the platform's N64 game library. The 1999 platformer will become available to subscribers with access to the N64 games collection.

Donkey Kong 64 was originally released for the Nintendo 64 console. Nintendo Switch Online offers a subscription service that provides access to classic games from older Nintendo systems, including the N64, Super Nintendo, and NES.

hero.headline: Packers Running Back Josh Jacobs Released From Jail, District Attorney Delays Charging Decision
hero.body:
Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs was released from jail after his arrest on domestic violence charges. The district attorney has not yet decided whether to file formal charges against the player.

Jacobs faced arrest on five charges, including felony strangulation, according to reports. The charges stem from an alleged domestic violence incident, though specific details about what occurred have not been disclosed publicly.

The Packers player was taken into custody and later released as the investigation continues. Law enforcement has not provided a timeline for when the district attorney's office will make a decision on whether to proceed with charges.

The felony strangulation charge represents the most serious allegation among the five charges Jacobs faced at the time of his arrest. Such charges typically carry significant legal consequences if prosecutors decide to move forward.

Jacobs joined the Packers and has been a key part of the team's backfield. His legal situation now creates uncertainty about his status with the franchise as the investigation unfolds.

The district attorney's office is reviewing evidence and determining whether sufficient grounds exist to formally charge Jacobs. This review process can take days or weeks depending on the complexity of the case and the evidence available to prosecutors.

Neither Jacobs nor his representatives have issued public statements about the arrest or the allegations. The Packers organization has also not commented on the situation or indicated what steps, if any, they plan to take regarding Jacobs' status with the team.

Domestic violence cases involving professional athletes often draw significant public attention and can result in league discipline separate from any criminal proceedings. The NFL has not announced whether it will conduct its own investigation into the matter.

The investigation remains active as authorities continue gathering information. Jacobs' release from jail does not indicate the outcome of the case, as prosecutors frequently release individuals while deciding whether to file charges.

cards.headline: Senate Bill Proposes College Sports Salary Cap and Transfer Limits
cards.teaser: Senators Ted Cruz and Maria Cantwell introduced bipartisan legislation to reform college athletics with new restrictions on player movement and compensation.
cards.body:
Senators Ted Cruz and Maria Cantwell have introduced a bipartisan bill addressing college sports reform. The legislation proposes a salary cap for athletes and limits on transfers, representing a significant intervention in how college athletics operate.

The bill seeks to enforce caps on athlete compensation and restrict how often players can transfer between schools. The legislation also targets coaching moves, specifically addressing situations like Lane Kiffin's recent jump to LSU. SEC leaders are discussing backup plans as the bill moves through Congress.

cards.headline: Dodgers Place Kike Hernandez Back on Injured List With Oblique Tear
cards.teaser: Kike Hernandez returned to the injured list after being diagnosed with a significant oblique tear just two games after his comeback.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Dodgers utility player Kike Hernandez was placed back on the injured list after medical tests revealed a significant oblique tear. The injury occurred just two games after Hernandez returned from a previous stint on the injured list.

Hernandez had made an emotional return to the lineup and contributed to a Dodgers victory over the Colorado Rockies in a seventh-inning surge. The team recalled Freeland from Triple-A to fill the roster spot. The timeline for Hernandez's return has not been announced.

cards.headline: SEC Officials Criticize College Football Playoff Committee's Strength of Schedule Explanation
cards.teaser: Leaders from the Southeastern Conference publicly challenged the College Football Playoff selection committee's methodology for evaluating team schedules.
cards.body:
SEC leaders have voiced strong disagreement with the College Football Playoff committee's explanation of how it measures strength of schedule. The criticism comes as debates intensify over which metrics should determine playoff selections.

The conference officials questioned the transparency and consistency of the committee's process for ranking teams based on their opponents' quality. The dispute reflects ongoing tensions about how the playoff system weighs different conferences and schedules when making its final selections.

cards.headline: Lamar Jackson Says Ravens Coaching Change Feels Like Fresh Start
cards.teaser: The Baltimore quarterback described the team's new coaching staff as reinvigorating and said his commitment to the Ravens remains strong.
cards.body:
Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson said the team's coaching change has brought renewed energy to the organization. Jackson described the transition as feeling like a breath of fresh air while maintaining that his commitment to Baltimore has never wavered.

Jackson declined to discuss ongoing contract negotiations but said he wants to leave the conversation about fully guaranteed contracts in the past. He praised new coordinator Declan Doyle for making his job easier. Jackson also confirmed he remains focused on the Ravens despite questions about his long-term future with the franchise.

hero.headline: Spielberg Says Hollywood Should Never Use AI as Final Word on Creative Decisions
hero.body:
Steven Spielberg spoke against using artificial intelligence in filmmaking during a recent appearance on Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson's IMO podcast. The director drew a clear line on where he believes AI should and should not be applied in creative industries.

Spielberg said he sees value in AI for solving medical problems but opposes its use in taking over the creative process in Hollywood. He stated that Hollywood should never use AI as the final word on anything creative, describing that as where he draws the line.

The director's comments add his voice to ongoing debates in the entertainment industry about the role of artificial intelligence in creative work. His position focuses on maintaining human control over artistic decisions while acknowledging potential benefits of AI in other fields.

Spielberg has directed numerous films over a career spanning more than five decades. His stance reflects concerns among many filmmakers about preserving human creativity and decision-making in an industry increasingly exploring technological tools.

The podcast appearance with Obama and Robinson provided a platform for Spielberg to address technology's expanding role in entertainment. His remarks specifically targeted the use of AI in creative decision-making rather than as a support tool.

The director's position distinguishes between AI applications he considers acceptable and those he views as crossing a boundary. He emphasized that creative choices should remain in human hands even as technology offers new capabilities to the film industry.

cards.headline: ABC News and National Geographic Lead News Emmy Winners
cards.teaser: ABC News won eight awards at the 47th annual News Emmys, with National Geographic close behind at seven wins.
cards.body:
ABC News led all networks at the 47th annual News Emmy Awards with eight wins. The network claimed the top prize for outstanding live news program for ABC World News Tonight With David Muir, repeating its victory from the previous year.

National Geographic won seven News Emmys, with multiple wins for Trafficked With Mariana van Zeller. Both networks are owned by Disney.

cards.headline: Student Criticizes CBS News While Accepting Mike Wallace Scholarship
cards.teaser: A scholarship winner used his acceptance speech at the News Emmys to publicly challenge CBS News direction.
cards.body:
Santiago Campos, a senior at District of Columbia International School in Washington, used his acceptance speech for the Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship at the News Emmys to criticize CBS News. He told the assembled audience that the network's recent direction undermines the legacy of the legendary journalist the scholarship commemorates.

Former CBS Evening News anchor Scott Pelley presented the award to Campos during the ceremony.

cards.headline: Obsession Breaks Box Office Pattern With Second Weekend Increase
cards.teaser: The film achieved a rare second-weekend box office spike, marking an unusual pattern for theatrical releases.
cards.body:
Obsession posted a box office increase in its second weekend of release, a performance pattern described as making history. The film became a breakout box office hit for the summer season.

The second-weekend spike represents a performance not seen since Sound of Freedom. The film's box office trajectory has drawn attention for defying typical weekend-to-weekend decline patterns that most theatrical releases follow.

cards.headline: Morris Day Denies Participation in Freedom 250 National Mall Concert
cards.teaser: The singer said he will not perform at a June concert on the National Mall despite being listed as a headliner by organizers.
cards.body:
Morris Day denied reports that he and the Time will perform at the Freedom 250 concert on the National Mall, calling them rumors. Organizers had announced him as headlining a show scheduled for June 27 as part of a 16-day patriotic fair in Washington.

Day stated it is a no for him regarding the event. The Freedom 250 festival is part of celebrations for the United States' 250th birthday and features other performers including Martina McBride, Flo Rida, and Vanilla Ice.

cards.headline: Rodrigo Addresses Criticism Over Recent Fashion Choices
cards.teaser: Olivia Rodrigo responded to online backlash about her clothing, saying people should not be held responsible for others sexualizing them.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo weighed in on controversy surrounding her recent outfits. The singer faced backlash from internet commenters who accused her recent clothing choices of both infantilizing and sexualizing her.

Rodrigo said people should not be responsible for some guy sexualizing them. Her comments addressed the criticism directly as she defended her fashion decisions amid the online debate about her appearance.

hero.headline: Justice Department opens criminal investigation into Trump accuser E. Jean Carroll
hero.body:
The Department of Justice has opened a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll, who accused President Trump of sexual assault, according to multiple reports. CNN first reported the investigation Wednesday night.

The probe focuses on whether Carroll committed perjury during a deposition as part of her two civil cases against Trump. Carroll won those civil cases, in which juries found Trump liable for sexual abuse and defamation.

The investigation represents a significant shift in the Justice Department's handling of matters related to Trump and his accusers. Carroll's legal victories against Trump in civil court resulted in substantial monetary damages.

The timing of the investigation has drawn attention, coming years after Carroll first publicly accused Trump of assault in the 1990s at a New York department store. Trump has repeatedly denied the allegations.

Carroll's attorney has not publicly commented on the reported investigation. The Justice Department typically does not confirm or deny ongoing investigations.

The perjury investigation appears to center on statements Carroll made under oath during depositions in her defamation and battery lawsuits against Trump. Those cases proceeded through federal court in New York.

The civil trials featured testimony from Carroll and other witnesses, along with evidence presented by both legal teams. Juries in both cases ruled in Carroll's favor, awarding her millions of dollars in damages.

The criminal investigation marks a new legal front in the long-running dispute between Carroll and Trump. Perjury charges require prosecutors to prove that a person knowingly made false statements under oath with intent to deceive.

Federal perjury cases can be difficult to prosecute, as they require clear evidence that the defendant deliberately lied rather than simply misremembered or misspoke. The Justice Department has not indicated what specific statements might be under scrutiny.

cards.headline: US military shoots down four Iranian drones, strikes launch site
cards.teaser: American forces intercepted drones targeting a commercial ship in the Strait of Hormuz and destroyed a ground control station.
cards.body:
The U.S. military intercepted four Iranian attack drones threatening a commercial vessel in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday and destroyed an Iranian ground control station in Bandar Abbas that was preparing to launch a fifth drone. U.S. Central Command confirmed the military action.

This marks the second such confrontation in 48 hours between the two nations. The incidents occur amid ongoing negotiations to end the three-month conflict and a fragile ceasefire between the U.S. and Iran.

cards.headline: Former judges ask court to investigate Trump IRS settlement
cards.teaser: A bipartisan group of former federal judges filed a request to reopen Trump's lawsuit against the tax agency.
cards.body:
A bipartisan group of former federal judges asked a federal court on Wednesday to reopen President Trump's lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service, contending that the administration bypassed judicial oversight by settling the dispute directly.

The $1.776 billion fund created through the settlement compensates alleged victims of what the administration calls "lawfare and weaponization." California Governor Gavin Newsom has announced plans to impose a 100% tax on any payouts received by state residents, seeking to counteract the fund's distribution.

cards.headline: Senator Andy Kim responds to criticism over detention facility protest
cards.teaser: The New Jersey Democrat defended his attendance at a demonstration outside a migrant detention center.
cards.body:
Senator Andy Kim fired back at Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin on Wednesday after Mullin criticized the senator for attending a protest outside a migrant detention facility in New Jersey. Kim said the issue was never about him personally.

During a cabinet meeting at the White House on Wednesday, Mullin said Kim complained about being hit by pepper ball spray at the protest. The exchange highlighted tensions between Democratic lawmakers and the Trump administration over immigration enforcement policies.

cards.headline: Zelensky asks Trump and Congress for Patriot missile interceptors
cards.teaser: The Ukrainian president said his country needs anti-missile defense systems to help end the conflict with Russia.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky appealed to President Trump and Congress on Wednesday for Patriot missile interceptors to strengthen Kyiv's air defenses against Russian attacks. Zelensky emphasized that while Ukraine has made progress defending against drone strikes, the country lacks the domestic capability to produce anti-missile defense systems.

The plea comes as Russia continues its assault on Ukrainian targets. Kyiv has achieved some success countering various types of drones but remains dependent on external support for advanced air defense capabilities needed to protect against ongoing Russian strikes.
